finding: .github/workflows/build.yml:20 The step downloads install.sh over the network, then verifies it against install.sha256. That checksum file is not in the repo, and if it were fetched from the same origin it would prove nothing. install.sha256 does not exist in the checkout, so sha256sum -c fails and the build always breaks. If someone adds a checksum fetched from tools.example.com, an attacker who controls that host controls both files, and sh install.sh runs attacker code in a job that later holds DEPLOY_KEY.

requirements.txt:2 --index-url pointing at an internal index replaces PyPI for the whole file, so requests and ourlib both resolve from it. The --index-url also sits after requests, which is misleading. pip install -r requirements.txt fetches every package, including requests==2.32.3, from pypi.internal.example. If that index proxies or lets others publish, an attacker can publish a malicious ourlib or requests. If it does not mirror PyPI, the install fails. Nothing is hash-pinned, because there is no --require-hashes. The safer form is --extra-index-url with hashes, or a private-only index with namespace control.

deploy.sh is not executable, so the Deploy step fails. The file is committed as mode 100644, and .github/workflows/build.yml:25 runs ./deploy.sh --key "$DEPLOY_KEY" with no chmod first. Every push to main fails with "Permission denied".

package-lock.json:11 Lockfile integrity values are placeholders (also line 16), and there is no package.json. package-lock.json:11 and :16 hold sha512-EXAMPLE and sha512-EXAMPLE2. A real sha512 integrity string is 88 base64 characters. The workspace has no package.json for the lock's root entry, and the root package lists no dependencies, yet two packages are locked. Traced, not run: no npm was available. npm ci has no package.json to install from. Even with one, the left-pad tarball's real hash will not match sha512-EXAMPLE, so npm aborts with EINTEGRITY. Where a tool skips the check, the lock pins nothing.

1. deploy.sh is committed without the executable bit
.github/workflows/build.yml, "Deploy" step: run: ./deploy.sh --key "$DEPLOY_KEY".

git diff shows deploy.sh as new file mode 100644, so the checked-out file isn't executable. The step fails with Permission denied every time it runs. Either chmod +x and commit the mode, or call it as sh ./deploy.sh.

Dockerfile:1 The image uses an unpinned base tag, runs as root, and runs COPY . /app before the dependency install, which defeats layer caching and bakes the whole context into the image. python:3.12-slim drifts between builds, so builds are not reproducible. Any change to any file reruns pip install. Anything in the build context, including .git and local secrets or .env files, is copied into the image because there is no .dockerignore. The container runs as root. Dockerfile line 3 also installs with no hash pinning.

package-lock.json:13 our-utils looks like an internal package but is resolved from the public npm registry. The integrity values for both packages are placeholders (sha512-EXAMPLE, sha512-EXAMPLE2). If our-utils is private, anyone can publish that name on public npm, which is a dependency-confusion takeover. npm ci fails on the invalid integrity strings. If the strings are not strictly validated, integrity checking is effectively absent.

deploy.sh:4 deploy.sh only echoes "deploying". It performs no deployment and ignores the --key argument that the workflow passes. The Deploy step reports success on every push to main while nothing is deployed. A green build is therefore misleading, and the key plumbing is dead code.

Dockerfile.base:3 COPY --from=build /app /app copies a path that the build stage never creates, because that stage is only a bare FROM. docker build -f Dockerfile.base fails with "/app: not found". The pinned digest looks like a placeholder, so it may also fail to resolve. The final image is scratch with no runtime.

build.yml:20-21 checks a checksum file that doesn't exist. The Install tool step runs sha256sum -c install.sha256 && sh install.sh. The step downloads only install.sh, and install.sha256 is not in the repo. The step fails on every push to main, and sh install.sh never runs.

Code review

I read the diff myself (git diff main...HEAD: 11 new files, one commit, and main is empty) and did not launch sub-agents. There is no CLAUDE.md in the repo, so I checked bugs only.
The --index-url lines in requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt.

Dockerfile:1 The deployed image uses a floating tag, while the other Dockerfile pins a digest. python:3.12-slim moves with every Debian and patch release. Dockerfile.base pins by digest, so the project's own standard is not applied to the image that is actually built. Two builds of the same commit a week apart pull different base layers. A regression or compromised upstream image reaches production with no diff in the repo, and rollback to the same commit does not restore the old image.

build.yml, "Install tool": sha256sum -c install.sha256 && sh install.sh. No install.sha256 exists in the tree, and the step never downloads one. sha256sum -c fails with "No such file", so the install and everything after it, including Deploy, never run.

Dockerfile.base:3 Dockerfile.base copies /app from a build stage that never creates it. Dockerfile.base:1 defines stage 'build' as python:3.12-slim with no RUN, COPY or WORKDIR. The stock python image has no /app directory. Line 3 then copies /app out of that stage into a scratch image. Line 1 also pins a digest of the form 0123456789abcdef... repeated, which is not a real image digest, so even the pull cannot resolve. docker build -f Dockerfile.base . fails: the pull of the digest returns 'not found', and (if it resolved) the COPY fails with '/app: not found'.

.github/workflows/safe.yml:22 lockedorg/tool@v1 is a mutable tag. actions.lock records a SHA for it, but GitHub Actions does not read that file, so the pin is never enforced. The owner moves v1 to a malicious commit, and the workflow runs it while TOKEN (API_TOKEN) is in scope. The lock file gives a false sense of pinning. The same step block also downloads tool.tgz and checks it against tool.sha256, which is neither in the repo nor from an independent source.

safe.yml:27-28 has the same problem with tool.sha256. The step downloads only tool.tgz, and tool.sha256 is not in the repo. The check job fails on every pull request. The validator couldn't read the two third-party actions' code, so it couldn't rule out one of them creating the file.

Filtered out: the package-lock.json placeholder integrity values (sha512-EXAMPLE, sha512-EXAMPLE2) were not validated. The repo has no package.json, and nothing runs npm, so npm ci can't fail on them here.

Nothing was posted, since --comment wasn't given, and no files were changed.

requirements-dev.txt:1 A second --index-url in the dev requirements file repeats the same dependency-confusion exposure for ourlib==1.0, and there are no hashes. pip install -r requirements-dev.txt trusts whatever the internal index serves for ourlib. With --extra-index-url it would instead take the highest version from either index. In either case a compromised or confused index delivers attacker code into dev and CI.

.github/workflows/build.yml:21 Checksum gate reads install.sha256, which is not in the repo, so the build job fails before Deploy. grep for 'sha256' over the whole tracked tree (git ls-files lists 11 files) finds install.sha256 and tool.sha256 only as arguments in build.yml:21 and safe.yml:28. Neither file exists, and the step downloads only install.sh / tool.tgz, not a checksum file. The run: shell is bash -e, so a failing sha256sum aborts the step. Push to main: the 'Install tool' step downloads install.sh, then 'sha256sum -c install.sha256' prints 'install.sha256: No such file or directory' and exits non-zero. 'Deploy' and the artifact upload never run, so main can never deploy. On every pull request, safe.yml 'Download and check' fails the same way on tool.sha256, so the check job is always red.

.github/workflows/build.yml:21 Checksum file install.sha256 is never downloaded and is not in the repo, so the build step fails on every push to main. build.yml:20 downloads only install.sh. build.yml:21 verifies it against install.sha256. A glob of the whole workspace shows no install.sha256 (nor tool.sha256 for safe.yml:28). The checkout at build.yml:11 can only supply files that are committed. GitHub's default bash shell runs with -e, so the failed sha256sum fails the step and the Deploy step at line 22 never runs. The same pattern is in safe.yml:28 (tool.sha256 is missing). Push to main. Step 'Install tool' runs: sha256sum prints 'install.sha256: No such file or directory' and exits 1. The job fails before 'Deploy' and 'upload-artifact'. The pull_request job in safe.yml fails the same way at 'Download and check' because tool.sha256 is absent.

.github/workflows/build.yml:25 deploy.sh is committed as mode 100644, so ./deploy.sh in the Deploy step fails with Permission denied. git ls-files -s shows 100644 for deploy.sh; ls -l shows -rw-r--r--. actions/checkout keeps the git mode. The step runs the script by path, not as 'sh deploy.sh'. Once the checksum step is fixed, the Deploy step runs './deploy.sh --key ...' and the shell returns 'Permission denied' (exit 126). The deploy fails on every push to main. This is a second, independent fix.

deploy.sh:4 deploy.sh deploys nothing and ignores --key, yet the workflow's Deploy step passes. build.yml:25 runs ./deploy.sh --key "$DEPLOY_KEY". deploy.sh has set -e, one echo and no argument handling, so it exits 0 whatever it is given. The secret is also passed as a command-line argument, so it is visible in the runner's process list for the life of the process, not only through the environment. Merge to main: the Deploy step goes green and the log says 'deploying'. No artifact is pushed anywhere. The team reads a green run as a shipped release.

.github/workflows/build.yml:25 DEPLOY_KEY is passed as a command-line argument (--key "$DEPLOY_KEY"), and deploy.sh never reads it. The key is visible in the process argument list (ps) to any process on the runner, including the unverified install.sh run earlier in the same job. It can also leak through shell tracing. deploy.sh ignores $@, so the secret is exposed for no benefit.

.github/workflows/triage.yml:12 A pull_request_target workflow with write permissions runs a third-party action and checks out the repo with default credentials persisted. safe-target.yml does the same. The checkout uses the default persist-credentials: true, so the write-scoped token stays in .git/config for later steps. The someorg/labeler step runs with that token on every PR event, including PRs from forks. If a later edit adds ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}, or the labeler reads PR-controlled files, the token is exposed to untrusted code. The SHA 1111… also looks like a placeholder that cannot resolve.

Dockerfile.base can't build. The build stage is only a FROM line, so it never creates /app, and COPY --from=build /app /app fails. The pinned digest (sha256:0123456789abcdef… repeated) is also not a real one, so the first FROM would fail before that.
